questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb as used in the sentence: 'The committee decided to CALL OFF the merger after discovering financial irregularities.'

options.option_text: to cancel or abandon something already planned
to postpone something to a later and unspecified date
to contact someone by telephone for further discussion
to invite participation from additional outside parties

questions.explanation: A is correct. CALL OFF means to cancel something. The discovery of irregularities led to the merger being abandoned entirely. B (postpone) is DEFER or PUT OFF. C (telephone) is CALL UP. D (invite) is unrelated. Note the difference: 'call off' cancels permanently; 'put off' merely delays.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'She had to COME TO TERMS WITH the fact that her application had been rejected.'

options.option_text: to accept a difficult or unpleasant reality
to negotiate new conditions with the decision-making body
to formally appeal against an unfavourable administrative decision
to understand the legal implications of a ruling or verdict

questions.explanation: A is correct. COME TO TERMS WITH means to accept or learn to live with something unpleasant. B (negotiate) confuses 'terms' in a contractual sense with the psychological sense of acceptance. C (appeal) is the opposite — it resists rather than accepts. D (understand legal implications) is a superficial reading that mistakes 'terms' for legal clauses.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The detective was able to PIECE TOGETHER what had happened from the witnesses' accounts.'

options.option_text: to reconstruct an account or explanation from separate fragments
to conduct a formal interview with multiple witnesses simultaneously
to compare conflicting testimonies and resolve inconsistencies
to arrange the physical evidence at a crime scene in order

questions.explanation: A is correct. PIECE TOGETHER means to assemble information from fragments to understand a complete picture. B (simultaneous interview) is unrelated. C (resolve inconsistencies) is related but PIECE TOGETHER doesn't imply resolving conflict — it implies assembling. D (arrange physical evidence) misreads 'piece together' literally as handling physical objects.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The government promised to CRACK DOWN ON illegal money lending in rural areas.'

options.option_text: to enforce regulations more strictly and take punitive action
to investigate the scale of a problem through official surveys
to negotiate a settlement with those engaged in unlawful activity
to introduce new legislation to regulate an existing practice

questions.explanation: A is correct. CRACK DOWN ON means to take severe or punitive action to suppress something. B (investigate) is preliminary, not punitive action. C (negotiate) would be REACH A SETTLEMENT. D (introduce legislation) is LEGISLATE AGAINST — it may accompany a crackdown but is not the meaning of the phrase itself.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'After years of failure, the entrepreneur eventually PULLED OFF an extraordinary turnaround.'

options.option_text: to succeed in doing something difficult or unexpected
to withdraw from a situation or arrangement at the last moment
to remove an obstacle that was preventing forward progress
to receive external recognition for a significant achievement

questions.explanation: A is correct. PULL OFF means to accomplish something difficult or improbable. B (withdraw at last moment) is PULL OUT, not PULL OFF. C (remove obstacle) is a physical, literal reading. D (receive recognition) is GAIN RECOGNITION — not the meaning of the phrasal verb.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The new manager quickly WEEDED OUT staff who were not meeting performance targets.'

options.option_text: to remove or eliminate undesirable elements from a group
to identify which employees needed additional training and support
to classify employees by performance into different categories
to provide incentives for employees who were underperforming

questions.explanation: A is correct. WEED OUT means to remove unwanted people or things from a group. The analogy is to gardening — removing weeds so the good plants can thrive. B (identify for training) is IDENTIFY — not the same as removing. C (classify) is CATEGORISE. D (provide incentives) is INCENTIVISE — the opposite of removing people.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The journalist DUG UP evidence of corruption that had been buried for decades.'

options.option_text: to discover information through determined research or investigation
to unearth physical artefacts during an archaeological survey
to exhume documents that were deliberately sealed in an archive
to challenge officially accepted accounts through public debate

questions.explanation: A is correct. DIG UP (used figuratively) means to uncover hidden or suppressed information through investigation. B (unearth physical artefacts) is the literal meaning — not what's intended here. C (exhume sealed documents) is too literal and specific. D (challenge accounts through debate) is DISPUTE — a different action.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The director had to ACCOUNT FOR the significant discrepancy in the quarterly budget.'

options.option_text: to give a satisfactory explanation for something
to prepare a detailed financial audit of all budget items
to take responsibility by resigning from a leadership position
to adjust future budgets to compensate for previous shortfalls

questions.explanation: A is correct. ACCOUNT FOR means to explain or justify something — particularly a gap, discrepancy, or absence. B (prepare a financial audit) is a specific accounting process, not the meaning of the phrasal verb. C (resign) is one possible consequence but not the meaning. D (adjust future budgets) is OFFSET or COMPENSATE.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The peace talks BROKE DOWN after neither side was willing to compromise on the key issues.'

options.option_text: to fail completely after making no progress
to reach a temporary suspension to allow both sides to consult
to collapse into open conflict after a negotiation attempt
to pause proceedings while waiting for senior officials to decide

questions.explanation: A is correct. BREAK DOWN (when applied to talks, systems, or relationships) means to fail completely and stop functioning. B (temporary suspension) is ADJOURN or RECESS. C (collapse into conflict) is what might FOLLOW a breakdown, but the phrasal verb itself doesn't imply armed conflict. D (pause for decisions) is STAND IN RECESS.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The opposition party tried to STIR UP public sentiment against the new taxation policy.'

options.option_text: to provoke or incite feelings or reactions in a group
to organise a formal campaign with petitions and public meetings
to circulate misleading information to confuse public opinion
to conduct a survey measuring levels of public approval or disapproval

questions.explanation: A is correct. STIR UP means to rouse or incite emotions or reactions — often intentionally. B (organise a formal campaign) is MOBILISE. C (circulate misleading information) is SPREAD MISINFORMATION — which may be one method, but is not the meaning of the phrasal verb. D (survey public opinion) is the opposite — measuring rather than creating sentiment.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The company decided to BRANCH OUT into renewable energy after years in the oil sector.'

options.option_text: to expand into a new area of activity beyond the existing one
to reduce dependence on fossil fuels for environmental reasons
to create a separate subsidiary focused on a different industry
to form a strategic partnership with another firm in a different sector

questions.explanation: A is correct. BRANCH OUT means to extend activities into a new area. B (reduce dependence) is a motivation, not the meaning. C (create a subsidiary) is a specific corporate action that may accompany branching out but is not what the phrasal verb means. D (form a partnership) is FORM AN ALLIANCE — a specific mode of expansion, not the phrase's meaning.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The Prime Minister was forced to BACK DOWN from the controversial policy after widespread protests.'

options.option_text: to withdraw from a position or demand under pressure
to transfer responsibility for the policy to a junior minister
to suspend implementation pending a judicial review of the policy
to announce a modified version of the policy as a compromise

questions.explanation: A is correct. BACK DOWN means to yield or retreat from a position under pressure. B (transfer responsibility) is DELEGATE — not a retreat. C (suspend pending review) is STAY IMPLEMENTATION — a legal action. D (announce a modified version) is REVISE — which could happen after backing down, but is a more specific action than the phrasal verb implies.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The CEO promised to LOOK INTO the allegations of workplace harassment immediately.'

options.option_text: to investigate or examine something carefully
to monitor ongoing developments within the organisation
to make a public statement responding to the allegations raised
to appoint an external authority to handle the complaint

questions.explanation: A is correct. LOOK INTO means to investigate or examine something — to enquire into it. B (monitor ongoing developments) is KEEP AN EYE ON. C (make a public statement) is RESPOND — not the same as investigating. D (appoint an external authority) is a specific possible action following an investigation, not the meaning of the phrasal verb.

questions.stem: Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb: 'The team had to FALL BACK ON their emergency reserves when the supply chain collapsed.'

options.option_text: to use something as a last resort when the primary option fails
to reduce operational capacity in response to a financial crisis
to retreat to an earlier and more familiar strategy or method
to seek assistance from an external agency or funding body

questions.explanation: A is correct. FALL BACK ON means to rely on something as a backup when the main option is unavailable. B (reduce capacity) is SCALE BACK — a different response. C (retreat to earlier strategy) is partially similar but FALL BACK ON specifically implies a reserve or safety net — not just any earlier method. D (seek external assistance) is REACH OUT FOR HELP.
